summary:
SP ratings are the story heading into the final slate: every rating model has SP hot over the last 14 days (R1 +9.5pts at 62%, R2 +9.5pts, R3 +6.0pts, all n=32) even while riding a 3-game losing streak in that category — a classic regression spot worth tracking closely rather than fading outright. Hitting is the other engine running hot across the board, topped by R4's absurd +16.6pts (69%, 22-10 over the last 14) and R3's +13.1pts (62%, 20-12). Meanwhile runs is the one category to treat skeptically: R1 is cold at -12.1pts (41%, 13-19) and R4 cold at -7.4pts, so any pick leaning hard on runs data alone today deserves a discount. Bullpen_fatigue is quietly strong everywhere too, all four ratings showing a 3-game win streak and +6.6 to +7.8pt bumps — that's the category to lean on when searching for tiebreakers.

Today's two-game slate keeps it simple and the model is unanimous: all four ratings like SDP over MIL, with R1 showing the largest edge at +1.09, tapering down to R4's +0.48 — still consensus, still worth full confidence given trends+sp is the best-performing category combo all season (58%, 363-263) and both of today's games feature starting pitching as a central storyline (Pivetta's matchup against a Dustin May-led Dodgers staff, Yamamoto vs. Sale in the night cap). On the LAD @ ATL side, every rating leans Dodgers but the deltas are razor-thin and negative-leaning in notation (R1 -0.14 down to R4 -0.09), meaning this is a soft consensus, not a confident one — treat it as a smaller units play. Worth noting LAD sits near the top of the team-when-liked leaderboard at 70% (37-16, n=53) with a strong-play record of 27-7 (+26.0u), so even a thin-delta Dodgers pick carries real backing from the team trend. SDP, by contrast, isn't in the current team leaderboard sample, but with four-rating agreement and SP/hitting both running hot, that's the stronger play of the two on the board today.
